pairs.question: Utra quaerunt homines, quae sciunt, an quae nesciunt?
pairs.derivation: Socrates' disjunctive interrogative (which do men seek, things they know or things they do not?) answered directly by Sisyphus with 'Utraque.' Speaker labels So./Sis. stripped; nothing trimmed.

pairs.question: Utrum igitur tibi Sisyphe faciendum videtur, si quis nesciat, quaerendum an discendum?
pairs.derivation: Disjunctive interrogative (should one who is ignorant seek or learn?) answered directly 'Discendum mehercule.' Speaker labels stripped; 'igitur' kept as author's word; nothing trimmed.

pairs.question: Sed utrum tibi propter hoc discendum potius, quam quaerendum videtur, quod citius, faciliusque invenire aliquis possit, si ab his qui sciunt, discat, quam si ipse imperitus quaerat: an hoc propter aliud?
pairs.derivation: Disjunctive interrogative kept whole so that 'propter hoc' (the reason: that one finds more quickly by learning from those who know) has its referent; answered 'Non, sed propter hoc.' Speaker labels stripped.
